summary: Daniel W. Kent is a scholar in religious and Buddhist studies who earned his Ph.D. from the University of Virginia. He held instructor posts at the University of Virginia and Mary Baldwin University, both attested in 2010.

Daniel Wojahn specializes in Tibetology and history/archaeology. He studied at the University of Leipzig (MA, 2013–2016) and University of Oxford (DPhil, 2019–2024). His positions include roles at Leipzig, Brill, Oxford, Bonn (2024), and Vienna (Associate Researcher, 2025).

Daniel Wright (1833–1902) was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at the University of St Andrews (~1849–1853) and served as a physician at the British Residency in Nepal from 1866 to 1876.

Daniela Berti works in Indology and religious studies. She studied at Sapienza University of Rome, University of Siena (PhD), and Paris Nanterre University (HDR). Her career includes posts at INALCO (2001–2003) and CNRS as a senior researcher / directrice de recherche.

Daniela Bevilacqua specializes in Indology and religious studies, having studied at Sapienza University of Rome and Paris Nanterre University (PhD). She has held posts at SOAS (2015–2020), University of Turin (2021), and Iscte – University Institute of Lisbon (2023).

Daniela De Simone specializes in history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. Holding degrees from Kendriya Hindi Sansthan, LSE, and University of Naples "L'Orientale" (PhD, 2007–2012), she has worked at the British Museum (2016–2020) and Ghent University (2021).

Daniela Rossella (born 1955) is an Indologist who studied at the University of Milan. She held positions at the University of Perugia (attested 2002), the University of Milan (attested 2003), and Ca' Foscari University of Venice.

Daniele Cuneo has held posts at the University of Cambridge (attested 2014), the University of Paris and the Sorbonne (both attested 2018), and as faculty at the University of Texas at Austin (attested 2026).
Danielle Feller is an Indologist who earned her PhD from the University of Lausanne in 2001. She studied under Ganesh U. Thite and her doctoral supervisor Johannes Bronkhorst.
Danny M.C. Ching is a researcher in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Sinology. He was a PhD student at Columbia University in 2023, with studies there attested into 2026.

Danping Long specializes in Indology and Buddhist studies. She is a doctoral student whose studies are attested at both the University of Munich and the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities in 2026.

Danuta Stasik (born 1956) is an Indologist who studied at the University of Warsaw under Maria Byrski (~1975–1980). In 1986, she became Chair of South Asian Studies in the Faculty of Oriental Studies at the University of Warsaw.

Daoquan Yu (1901–1992) was a scholar of Tibetology and linguistics. He studied at Cheeloo University (~1920–1924) and under Jacques Bacot (~1934–1937), later serving as a professor at Minzu University of China (~1953–1986).

Dasharatha Sharma (1903–1976) was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. Educated at the University of Delhi, he held positions at Hindu College, University of Delhi, Jai Narain Vyas University, and directed the Rajasthan Oriental Research Institute (~1969–1974).

Daud Ali (born 1964) is an Indology and history/archaeology scholar. He studied at William & Mary and the University of Chicago under Ronald Inden. He taught history at SOAS (~1995–2009) and became an Associate Professor at the University of Pennsylvania in 2009.
David A. Dilworth (born 1934) is a scholar in philosophy and Japanology. He studied under teachers Masao Abe and Valdo H. Viglielmo (1968).

David A. Hall works in Buddhist studies and Japanology. He studied under Shoshin Ichishima (1976) and earned a doctorate from UC Berkeley (1990). He was a visiting scholar at Taisho University (1977) and department chair at Montgomery College (attested 2019).

David Aberle (1918–2004) studied at Harvard University (~1937–1940), Columbia University (~1940–1950), and the University of New Mexico. He held a post at the University of British Columbia (~1967–1983).
David Azzopardi is a scholar in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied for his PhD at SOAS University of London under doctoral supervisor Kate Crosby (attested 2010).

David B. Gray works in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and religious studies. He earned his Ph.D. at Columbia University under Robert A. F. Thurman and Ryuichi Abe. His career includes posts at Columbia, Rice University, and Santa Clara University (attested 2005–2017).
